newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak monopoly to launch SKK1.5bln bond.
newsitem.headline: Slovak monopoly to launch SKK1.5bln bond.

text.p: Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. (SE), Slovakia's state energy utility, will launch a seven-year, 1.5 billion crown bond issue in early December, lead-manager Slovenska Sporitelna a.s. said on Thursday.
A senior Sporitelna official told Reuters the bonds would carry an annual fixed coupon rate of 12.3 percent.
The rate of the issue of 10,000 crown denominated bonds is set at 100 percent of the nominal value, said Sporitelna's treasurer Ivan Benda. Interest on the bonds will be paid annually.
"The issue will be launched in early December on the domestic market, and as the lead-manager we want to form its underwriting syndicate with the largest domestic and foreign banks," he said.
"This would be the largest and first seven-year corporate bond issue placed on a domestic market so far."
Benda added that the syndication strategy had not been defined yet, but that Sporitelna would folow "standard" international proceedures.
SE is Slovakia's fifth largest company by revenue, which totalled 27.1 billion crowns in 1995.

Funds from the bond will be used for general purposes, including operating innovations and refinancing old loans, but will not be used for the completion of the Mochovce nuclear power plant, Benda added.
SE is still fully owned by the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund, and last year the government declared it a strategic asset which should not be privatised.
